problem: Prior semantic audio-visual navigation (SAVi) methods have no explicit mechanism for domain knowledge about object and region semantics. Their benchmarks only test unheard clips of known sounding objects, so generalisation to truly novel sounding objects is never assessed.
motivation: Humans use background knowledge (e.g. a smoke alarm is likely in the kitchen) to search for unfamiliar sound sources. Injecting a scene prior over object-object, object-region and region-region relations should let agents reason sound -> object -> region and generalise to novel sounds and houses. A new task split with unheard sounding objects is needed to measure this.
key_idea: Add a knowledge graph of object/region co-occurrence, encoded by two GCN-based Graph Encoder Networks (one visual, one audio) and pre-trained classifiers, to a Scene Memory Transformer RL policy so the agent can reason about novel sounding objects.
insight: The gains come mostly in unheard-sound settings: Seen Houses/Unheard Sounds SR rises from 21.7 (SAVi) to 37.8, and Unseen Houses/Unheard Sounds SR from 15.3 to 34.4. On heard sounds it only matches SAVi. Ablations show GEN^v helps most when sounds are heard (SH/HS SR 73.2 for only-GEN^v vs 64.4 for only-GEN^b), while GEN^b helps most when sounds are unheard. Using the estimated DRR as a dynamic weight hurts, so the fixed 0.5 average is better (UH/US SR 34.4 vs 27.2).
method: Knowledge graph: an undirected graph over 21 objects and 24 regions (|V|=45), built from MP3D semantic labels. Object-object edges come from frequent co-occurrence in a region, object-region edges are derived from object-object edges, and region-region edges from shared connected objects. Thresholds are frequency-based.

Modular pre-training: a ResNet-18 audio classifier (21 objects, 1.5M simulated spectrograms, 97.3% test accuracy) and a ResNet-18 vision multi-label classifier (21 objects + 24 regions, 45,233 filtered images). Both are frozen during policy training. Audio predictions are smoothed over time with a factor of 0.5.

Graph Encoder Networks (GEN^v, GEN^b): 3-layer GCNs over the knowledge graph. Node inputs are GloVe word embeddings (300-d) concatenated with classifier scores, and outputs are 64-d. GEN^v output goes into scene memory; GEN^b output is used to attend to that memory.

Location predictor with DRR: a simplified ResNet-18, trained jointly with the policy, that predicts the relative (dx, dy) of the sound source and the direct-to-reverberant ratio as an auxiliary task. Estimates are aggregated over time with an exponential average (delta=0.5) and propagated using pose changes.

Scene Memory Transformer policy: memory stores [vision embedding, GEN^v embedding, pose, previous action] (size 150 in stage 2). A transformer encoder processes memory, and a decoder attends to it with the audio-GEN embedding and location estimate to give the state for an actor-critic head.
Training: DD-PPO for 300M steps in two SMT stages (memory size 1, then 150 with vision networks frozen). Reward is +10 for success, +1/-1 for geodesic distance change, and -0.01 per step.
New task split: evaluation in 4 conditions (seen/unseen houses x heard/unheard sounds) using 68 seen and 17 unseen houses, with 16 heard and 5 unheard sounding objects.

setting.backbone: SMT transformer policy with GCN Graph Encoder Networks and ResNet-18 audio/vision classifiers (trained from scratch, ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18), trained with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: 367,155 training episodes in 68 MP3D houses via SoundSpaces; vision classifier on 45,233 simulator images; audio classifier on 1.5M simulated spectrograms; MP3D semantic labels for the knowledge graph
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth (128x128) + binaural audio + pose relative to start
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveForward, TurnLeft, TurnRight, Stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (MP3D semantic labels are used only for pre-training and knowledge graph construction)

numbers.eval_set_note: Seen Houses, Heard Sounds; 1,000 episodes; 68 seen houses, 16 heard sounding objects (paper's own split)
numbers.backbone: SMT + GEN^v + GEN^b + DRR location predictor

numbers.eval_set_note: Seen Houses, Unheard Sounds; 1,000 episodes; 5 unheard sounding objects (paper's own split)
numbers.backbone: SMT + GEN^v + GEN^b + DRR location predictor

numbers.eval_set_note: Unseen Houses, Heard Sounds; 1,000 episodes; 17 unseen houses (paper's own split)
numbers.backbone: SMT + GEN^v + GEN^b + DRR location predictor

numbers_note: Custom SoundSpaces splits defined by the paper (seen/unseen houses x heard/unheard sounds); none is an official split. The 'val' and 'val-unseen' labels are approximations. Metrics include SNA and SWS in addition to standard ones.
results: SAVEN beats SAVi, AudioGoal and AudioObjectGoal in every condition except Seen Houses/Heard Sounds, where it roughly ties SAVi (SR 70.2 vs 67.2, but SPL 52.8 vs 53.6). In Unseen Houses/Unheard Sounds, SR is 34.4 vs 15.3 for SAVi. In Seen Houses/Unheard Sounds, SR is 37.8 vs 21.7 for SAVi.
limitations: The knowledge graph is built only from MP3D object-region co-occurrence and lacks sound-object relations, so the audio GEN is not pre-trained on sound semantics.
Absolute success on unseen houses and unheard sounds is still low (about 34% SR), and there are failure modes with repeated same-class objects and collisions.
Only 5 unheard sounding objects and 17 unseen houses are tested, with a single random split and no seeds or variance reported; the knowledge graph is restricted to 21 objects and 24 regions.
builds_on: Yang et al. visual semantic navigation priors
